Many small businesses struggle to see a return on their marketing investments
Blogging for small business does work, but not in the way most people think.
Let’s be honest: most small business owners get caught up in the trap of tracking metrics that don’t actually reflect business growth.
Website clicks, social media likes, and blog post views - they all look good on a spreadsheet
The key is to shift your focus from these vanity metrics to what truly matters: calls, leads
They’re about answering the specific questions your potential customers are asking when they’re searching for your services.
For example, if you own a landscaping business in Austin, Texas
not a detailed explanation of different types of irrigation systems.
A well-written blog post that addresses a local search query will naturally feed into your GBP
When someone searches for “best pizza near me
” your blog post about “the best pizza places in {Your Town}” can signal to Google that you’re a relevant local business.
A steady stream of relevant content keeps Google seeing you as active and engaged in your community.
Consider a content calendar to plan your topics and schedule your posts.
When you’re writing your blog posts, focus on answering exact local search queries.
Instead, write about the specific problems you solve in your area.
“How to fix a leaky faucet in {Your City}” is far more effective than “Tips for Plumbing.
” Think about the common questions you hear from customers and address them directly in your blog posts.
Don’t get caught up in chasing website clicks if they’re not translating into calls.
Focus on measuring the number of calls you receive as a direct result of your blog content.
If you’re not getting calls, your content isn’t local enough.
